topic: How to Paste Your Schema So ChatGPT Stops Inventing Column Names

market_analysis.why_now: Millions of non-technical workers are pasting database questions into ChatGPT daily and getting back confident SQL with completely hallucinated column names like 'customer_id' when their table actually uses 'cust_no'. This is the number one reason beginners lose trust in AI-generated SQL and give up.
market_analysis.target_learner: A non-technical office worker or analyst who has access to a database, has tried asking ChatGPT to write SQL for them, and got burned by made-up column names they had to debug
market_analysis.learner_goal: Copy their real database schema and paste it into ChatGPT so every AI-generated query uses the actual column names from their database
market_analysis.competition_gap: Most prompt-engineering content is abstract and talks about 'providing context' without showing the exact 3-second copy-paste move that fixes hallucinated columns. Nobody shows the hilarious before-and-after of ChatGPT confidently using a column that does not exist.
market_analysis.platform_fit: TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts — this is a single visual gag (fake column names) followed by a satisfying one-move fix, perfect for short-form dopamine content where the payoff lands in under 90 seconds

content_structure.hook: ChatGPT just wrote you a perfect SQL query — except the column 'customer_email' does not exist anywhere in your database.
content_structure.core_promise: One paste fixes hallucinated column names forever.

lessons.title: One Paste to Kill Fake Column Names
lessons.learning_objective: By the end of this lesson the learner will be able to copy a CREATE TABLE statement from their database tool and paste it into a ChatGPT prompt so the AI uses real column names instead of inventing them.

scenes.what_learner_sees: Split screen: left side shows a ChatGPT conversation where the user asks 'write me a query to find customers who have not ordered in 90 days' and ChatGPT responds with a beautiful query referencing 'customer_email', 'last_order_date', and 'orders_table'. Right side shows the actual database schema where the columns are named 'cust_eml', 'lst_ord_dt', and the table is called 'tbl_ord_hist'. Red X marks slam onto each wrong name one by one.
scenes.what_learner_hears: Look at this. I asked ChatGPT for a query and it wrote something gorgeous. One problem — not a single one of these column names is real. It literally made them up. 'customer_email'? My database calls that 'cust_eml' because Dave from IT set it up in 2007 and Dave did not believe in vowels.
scenes.transition_to_next: Hard cut with a record-scratch sound effect

scenes.what_learner_sees: Screen recording: the creator opens their database tool, right-clicks a table, clicks 'Copy CREATE TABLE statement' (or highlights a schema definition), then switches to ChatGPT, pastes the schema at the top of the prompt with the text 'Here is my actual schema:' followed by the same natural language question. ChatGPT responds with a query that now uses the exact ugly real column names. A green checkmark appears on every column name. The query is correct.
scenes.what_learner_hears: Here is the fix and it takes three seconds. Go to your database, grab the CREATE TABLE statement — that is the thing that lists every real column name. Paste it into ChatGPT before your question. That is it. Now look — 'cust_eml', 'lst_ord_dt', 'tbl_ord_hist'. Every single column name is real. ChatGPT does not have to guess anymore because you gave it the cheat sheet. Stop letting the AI improvise. Paste your schema.

lessons.key_takeaway: Always paste your real CREATE TABLE statement into ChatGPT before asking for SQL — it cannot hallucinate column names if you hand it the real ones.

exercise_file_plan.purpose: A realistic ugly-but-real CREATE TABLE statement with abbreviated column names that the learner can paste into ChatGPT to practice the technique themselves

production_notes.hands_on_ratio: 10% — viewer mostly watches the demo and laughs at the hallucinated names, then optionally tries it with the sample schema file
